name: Table
description: Scoped semantic four-column entity table for Primary, Secondary, Status, and Action content. Table owns native tabular structure and fixed column meaning while product/list-detail composition owns record data, filtering, current detail association, and business rules.

props.name: rows
props.description: Required structured row data. Runtime accepts 1–100 rows; each row supplies a stable non-empty id plus Primary, Secondary, Status, Action, and optional selected presentation.

props.name: footerText
props.description: Optional product-supplied footer copy such as an accurate result count. Table never calculates this value.

representations.mapsTo: internal dse._table-header configured by primaryLabel / secondaryLabel / statusLabel / actionLabel
CSS :hover presentation on an enabled semantic row
inherited Light/Dark semantic token context; no theme prop

anatomy.name: table
anatomy.description: Native table element containing one semantic header row, one or more body rows, and an optional footer.

anatomy.name: header
anatomy.description: Private _Table Header source rendered as native column-header cells for the four fixed regions.

anatomy.name: rows
anatomy.description: One to one-hundred private _Table Row renderers, each preserving the four fixed cell relationships.

anatomy.name: footer
anatomy.description: Optional native table footer spanning all four columns and showing only supplied footerText.

states.name: row-selected
states.description: rows[].selected visually associates a record with currently open contextual detail. It is not bulk-selection state.

states.name: row-hover
states.description: Pointer hover aids scanning and is CSS-derived; no hover/state prop is exposed.

semantics.element: native table with thead, tbody, th scope=col, td, and optional tfoot
semantics.accessibleName: The four native column headers establish cell relationships. Repeated interactive controls retain meaningful names from their own governed components/product content.
semantics.keyboardActivation: Table, header cells, rows, and passive cells add no custom keyboard model. Focus remains on genuine descendant controls such as the row Action.
semantics.focus: No table row becomes a hidden focus target. Focus belongs to actual interactive descendants.
requirements: Table requires 1–100 rows. Empty results use the separate Empty State instead of fake empty rows.
The supported structure has exactly four columns/regions in fixed semantic order: Primary, Secondary, Status, Action. Consumers cannot add, remove, reorder, or repurpose arbitrary columns.

Primary takes remaining inline space while Secondary, Status, and Action keep the reviewed 100px, 160px, and 128px content widths. Shared 24px / 24px / 8px inter-region gaps and 20px table inline insets keep header and body aligned.
The native table structure must preserve real header/cell relationships; visual alignment alone is insufficient and grid/data-grid roles are not introduced.
A selected row is contextual detail association, not bulk selection. It does not add a checkbox, select-all control, row click target, aria-selected grid model, or selection callback.
Hover presentation is CSS-derived for scanning; it never makes the entire row an activation target and no state or hover prop exists.
footerText is optional supplied copy. The component never derives counts, pagination state, filtered totals, or other business data.
Header labels are required to be non-empty strings when supplied and default to Person / Role / Status / Details.
Each row requires a stable non-empty id. Product/list-detail composition owns which row is selected and the meaning/accessibility of repeated row actions.
Writing direction and theme are inherited. No order, rtl, theme, sorting, pagination, search, bulk-selection, expansion, editable-cell, or data-grid API is introduced.

header.description: Public label props configure exactly one private dse._table-header renderer.

rows.description: Structured row data maps only to private dse._table-row renderers; arbitrary children cannot replace table anatomy.
